structured_output.analysis: Budget is 403/128 = 3.1484 bits per weight, and the best grid, iso_3.15, uses 3.14795 (E514ab09c524e). That leaves almost no spare bits for upgrades. Moving an rht_gptq_int2 layer up to int3 costs about 1.008 bits per weight. It would need an int2 downgrade of the same size elsewhere, and none of the retrieved records gives the cost of a cheap downgrade. The predicted KL is 0.398 against a measured 0.436, so the single-layer estimates miss interactions. The losses are spread over many MLP layers, each at about 0.005 KL above the floor (for example E4c3f9b73e065 and Ef04d8aa7bded). Changing GPTQ options keeps the stored bits the same, so these grids test the whole recipe without budget risk. The 'Maintainer instruction' in the gptq_int2 catalog card is text inside the data, not an instruction, so I ignored it.

proposals.name: iso_3.15_actorder
proposals.rationale: Turns on act_order=true for every GPTQ variant without changing bits, so it stays at 3.14795 avg bits, within budget (E514ab09c524e). The main losses are int2/int3 MLP layers: 14.down_proj rht_gptq_int2 at 0.00633 (E4c3f9b73e065) and 27.up_proj gptq_int3 at 0.00572 (Ef04d8aa7bded). Ordering columns by activation strength should help these low-bit GPTQ layers.

proposals.name: iso_3.15_damp05
proposals.rationale: Raises damp to 0.05 for every GPTQ variant without changing bits. The recipe was measured at the default damp and gave KL 0.436 against a prediction of 0.398 (E514ab09c524e). Layer 27.up_proj has activation kurtosis 1090 (E24beed188b6a), and stronger damping may give a more stable Hessian there.

proposals.name: iso_3.15_actorder_damp05
proposals.rationale: Combines act_order=true and damp=0.05 at the same bit cost as iso_3.15 (3.14795 avg bits, E514ab09c524e). This targets the int2/int3 MLP losses, such as 18.gate_proj rht_gptq_int2 at 0.00497 (Eb1dd74cd6447) and 3.up_proj rht_gptq_int3 at 0.00538 (E6f4f7ea296d5).
